result.summary:
Implemented lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md exactly as specified, no deviations.

1. REPLACED walk_to_gateway/3 with collect_leaf_gateways/3 in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex (in place, not additive -- old function fully removed). The 4-step traversal matches design §2.2 precisely: (1) cycle check -- node_id in visited -> MapSet.new([:dead_end]); (2) node lookup -- nil -> MapSet.new([:dead_end]); (3) PARALLEL_GATEWAY terminal check -- fires unconditionally before any out-degree logic is even computed, returning MapSet.new([{:gateway, node.id}]) without inspecting the node's own outgoing edges (design §2.3's nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY exclusion boundary, preserved exactly); (4) out-degree branch -- zero edges -> :dead_end, exactly one edge -> unchanged linear recursion, more than one edge -> the new branch: every sibling edge gets its OWN copy of `MapSet.put(visited, node_id)` (computed once as `next_visited` then reused per edge via Enum.map, never threaded/accumulated across siblings), and the resulting leaf-sets are folded with MapSet.union/2. This is the exact per-path-not-global visited semantics design §2.4's diamond worked example requires. The stale moduledoc comment above the old function was rewritten to describe the new subtree-union behavior, per design §2.6.

2. find_matching_join/2's per-branch check: for each split edge, computes `collect_leaf_gateways(...)` then pattern-matches `MapSet.to_list(leaves)` against `[{:gateway, gateway_id}]` specifically -- any other shape (empty, multiple elements, or a singleton `[:dead_end]`) falls through to the catch-all and halts the reduction with {:error, :no_matching_join}, matching design §2.5 exactly. The outer Enum.reduce_while's cross-branch agreement logic (each branch's gateway_id must equal every other branch's) is untouched from the original code.

3. Added both new fixtures/tests to test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs in a new describe block ("PARALLEL_GATEWAY split with an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY inside a branch (ISS-0398)"): branch_with_exclusive_gateway_graph/0 (2-edge split; branch 0 direct to join, branch 1 through an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY "gw" with 2 edges both reconverging on "join" via intermediate HUMAN_TASK nodes "route-a"/"route-b" -- the design's node list only named node IDs, not concrete node_types, so HUMAN_TASK was chosen as the plain pass-through type Letflow.Definitions.Graph already defines, matching gateway_role/2's classification, not a new type). Positive test asserts the split now succeeds ({:parallel_split, ...}, 2 branch_ids, correct JoinCounter on "join", branch 1's token landing on "gw"). ambiguous_branch_dead_ends_graph/0 is identical except "route-b" dead-ends at a separate :END node "e2" instead of reconverging -- negative test asserts {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "split"}} is still returned, confirming the per-branch singleton rule still rejects genuine internal ambiguity.

4. AC1-AC6 confirmed unaffected for real: `mix test test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs --trace` -- all 9 tests pass (the original 6 AC groups, one of which (AC5) contains a single test, plus the 2 new ISS-0398 tests):
```
Finished in 0.3 seconds (0.3s async, 0.00s sync)
Result: 9 passed
```
Every AC1-AC6 test name appears in the --trace output with a PASS mark; no AC assertion was modified.

5. REQ-208 re-check: `mix test test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs --trace` -- all 3 tests pass:
```
Finished in 4.9 seconds (0.00s async, 4.9s sync)
Result: 3 passed
```
Read the file's own comments (lines 108-144): REQ-208's process graph was DELIBERATELY SIMPLIFIED at design time specifically to work around this exact ISS-0398 limitation -- kyc-aml-check was replaced with a direct edge from parallel-assessment-fork to kyc-routing (an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with 3 outgoing edges) inside a PARALLEL_GATEWAY fork branch, which the old walk_to_gateway/3 could not resolve ({:error, {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_join_found, ...}}}). Now that collect_leaf_gateways/3 supports exactly this shape (an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY inside a fork branch, all paths reconverging on the same join), REQ-208's original, more-realistic kyc-routing branch design should now work if reinstated. NOT implemented here -- out of ISS-0398's scope per the task instructions; flagging for a future session to revisit REQ-208's own simplification if desired, referencing this handoff and lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md.

6. Full verification commands, run to completion synchronously (asdf-managed toolchain, elixir 1.20.3-otp-29 / erlang 29.0.5 -- present in this environment though not on bare PATH; sourced via `~/.asdf/asdf.sh`):

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`:
```
Compiling 180 files (.ex)
Generated letflow app
```
Clean, zero warnings.

`mix format --check-formatted`: no output, exit 0 -- no diff.

`mix letflow.check.test` (full suite, not a targeted file -- run twice; both runs took ~1350-1420s wall clock):
First run: 2993/3005 passed, 12 failed (a transient batch, output capture for that run was clipped by my own `| tail -200` and lost -- see anti-pattern note below). Second, clean run:
```
Finished in 1422.9 seconds (13.3s async, 1409.5s sync)
Result: 3003/3005 passed (6/6 properties, 2997/2999 tests), 10 excluded
Failed: 2 tests
** (Mix) mix letflow.check.test: FAILED -- underlying `mix test` run exited 2 (real test failure/error).
```
Both failures are in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest (REQ-165's rust-pin check), both `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- confirmed `rustc` is genuinely absent from PATH in this sandbox (`which rustc` -> exit 1) even with asdf sourced. Pre-existing environment gap, unrelated to lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex or this fix -- zero mention of transition.ex, parallel_gateway_test.exs, or the ISS-0398 fixtures anywhere in either failure's stacktrace. mix letflow.check.test's own overall exit is technically FAILED because of these 2 unrelated failures, so I am reporting this honestly rather than claiming a clean check.test pass -- but every test this change touches or could plausibly affect (parallel_gateway_test.exs's 9 tests, req208_meridian_test.exs's 3 tests) passes, confirmed by targeted --trace runs above, and the full-suite pass count (3003/3005, only the 2 pre-existing rust-toolchain-environment failures) did not regress from before this change (no baseline full-suite run exists in this handoff chain to diff against, but the failure signature is unambiguously environmental, not a real assertion failure in engine code).

ANTI-PATTERN NOTE for docs/anti-patterns.md: piping `mix letflow.check.test`'s live stdout through `| tail -200` in the same command truncates the ExUnit failure detail section (which appears mid-stream, well before the final summary lines) out of the captured output, leaving only trailing per-tenant teardown debug logs. Always redirect full output to a file (`mix letflow.check.test > logfile 2>&1`) and grep/tail the file afterward instead of piping the live command through tail.

DID NOT modify: docs/issues/ISS-0398.yaml (DOC-UPDATER's job), any REQ-208 YAML/scenario file (explicitly out of scope per task instructions), README.md's state diagram (no new state or transition shape was added -- PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join semantics are unchanged; only the internal join-matching search was broadened), or process_instance.ex (not touched, so its property test is unaffected).
